reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 RANDOM's optional argument-1, when written, must be an integer (§1989:A.2.2 AR4) that is zero or positive, and its value seeds a new pseudo-random sequence: the compiler must refuse a non-integer argument form, accept integer forms, and at run time restart the sequence from the seed so the same seed reproduces the same sequence; a negative value is a value violation whose result is undefined.

reader.edition-search: Same greps as the other integer rows, plus the runtime Random(Int128) (no edition input) and FlagConformancePass.Flag85.cs#FlagFunctionCall85, which is the >>FLAG-85 GR4 e detector of a 2002+ directive and is not on the --std 85 path.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the same integer screen and the same runtime seed at every edition. The parse of RANDOM followed by a parenthesized expression inside a multi-argument function differs between 1985 and 2002 (FLAG-85 e), which is the format rule, not AR1.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf38_03 covers seeding; pb5886-random-seed-quotient covers a quotient refusal. Not exercised by the witnesses at 85: scaled item, numeric function, alphanumeric operand refusals and seed reproducibility against an argument-less continuation; probes cover them.

reader.notes: The seed is used as given (seed AND 0x7FFFFFFF, the identity on 0..2^31-1), so the 0..32767 floor yields distinct sequences, and re-seeding with 0 reproduced the first value. A negative seed at run time records an argument error and returns 0, which the undefined-result rule permits.
